---
title: "Input QC flags"
format:
  html:
    page-layout: full
execute:
  echo: false
---

The flags the input arrived with, before anything on this site compares
them: every observation of each product, counted by the value of its
temperature or salinity flag. The regional summary reports of the
[Arctic](https://aiqc-hub.github.io/arc-report/),
[Baltic](https://aiqc-hub.github.io/bal-report/) and
[Mediterranean](https://aiqc-hub.github.io/med-report/) give the same counts
one product at a time, with the flags by platform and over time; this page
puts them side by side. The
[exploratory data analysis](https://aiqc-hub.github.io/aiqc-report/) behind
those reports shows the fraction of bad flags per profile and how the flags
change over the years.

**This page counts every profile**, on land and in delayed mode too. The
Depth page leaves land profiles out of the analyses after it, and the
Delayed mode page sets profiles apart by their data mode; this one
describes the input as it is, not a subset that an analysis compares.

```{ojs}
//| output: false
app = import(new URL("assets/js/app.js", document.baseURI).href)
meta = app.loadAnalyses()
name = (id) => app.datasetName(meta, id)
table = app.analysisTable
byDataset = (a, b) => app.datasetOrder(meta, a.dataset_id) - app.datasetOrder(meta, b.dataset_id)
variableLabel = (n) => meta.variables.find((v) => v.name === n)?.label ?? n
byVariable = (a, b) =>
  meta.variables.findIndex((v) => v.name === a.variable) -
  meta.variables.findIndex((v) => v.name === b.variable)
flags = meta ? app.loadAnalysisTable("input_flags") : null

// The regional report page of each product and variable, where there is one.
// The ids are those of config/test_nrt.yaml; another configuration simply
// gets no links.
reportPrefix = new Map([
  ["ar_ar", "arc-report/ar_"],
  ["ar_gl", "arc-report/ar_gl_"],
  ["cora_ar", "arc-report/ar_cora_"],
  ["bo_bo", "bal-report/bo_"],
  ["cora_bo", "bal-report/bo_cora_"],
  ["mo_mo", "med-report/mo_"],
  ["mo_gl", "med-report/mo_gl_"],
  ["cora_mo", "med-report/mo_cora_"]
])
function reportLink(row) {
  const prefix = reportPrefix.get(row.dataset_id);
  if (!prefix) return document.createTextNode("");
  const link = document.createElement("a");
  link.href = `https://aiqc-hub.github.io/${prefix}${row.variable}_qc.html`;
  link.textContent = "QC page";
  return link;
}

// How the site reads a flag value, from each variable's lists in
// meta.json: the heading of a column says it once when every variable
// reads the value the same way.
function flagClass(spec, flag) {
  if (flag !== null && spec.bad_flag_values.includes(flag)) return "counted as bad";
  if (flag === null || spec.missing_flag_values.includes(flag)) return "no input flag";
  return "counted as good";
}
function flagTitle(flag) {
  const read = [...new Set(meta.variables.map((v) => flagClass(v, flag)))];
  return read.length === 1
    ? `On this site: ${read[0]}`
    : meta.variables.map((v) => `${v.label}: ${flagClass(v, flag)}`).join("; ");
}

flagKey = (flag) => (flag === null ? "none" : `flag ${flag}`)

// The site glosses only the values the IOC/Argo scheme fixes. The regional
// reports also name 5 to 8, as the Copernicus in situ products use them,
// and this page is about those products, so it names them too.
REPORT_MEANINGS = new Map([
  [5, "value changed"],
  [6, "below detection limit"],
  [7, "in excess of quoted value"],
  [8, "interpolated"]
])
flagHeading = (flag) =>
  REPORT_MEANINGS.has(flag) ? `${flag} (${REPORT_MEANINGS.get(flag)})` : app.flagWithMeaning(flag)
wide = flags
  ? app.widen(flags, {
      index: ["dataset_id", "variable"], column: "original_flag", value: "n_obs",
      name: flagKey
    }).sort((a, b) => byDataset(a, b) || byVariable(a, b))
  : []
// Every flag value any product uses, in order, with no flag last.
flagValues = [...new Set((flags ?? []).map((r) => r.original_flag))]
  .sort((a, b) => (a === null) - (b === null) || a - b)
withTotals = wide.map((row) => ({
  ...row,
  n_obs: flagValues.reduce((sum, f) => sum + row[flagKey(f)], 0)
}))
```

```{ojs}
meta === null ? app.analysesMissing() : html``
```

## The flags per product

One row per product and variable. The flag values follow the IOC/Argo
scheme, with the meanings of 5 to 8 as the regional reports give them for
these products; pointing at a heading says how the rest of the site reads
the value. "none" is an observation the input gives no flag at all.

```{ojs}
viewof flagUnit = Inputs.radio(["Share of the observations", "Observations"], {
  value: "Share of the observations",
  label: "Show"
})
```

```{ojs}
meta ? table(withTotals, [
  { key: "dataset_id", label: "Product", align: "left", format: name },
  { key: "variable", label: "Variable", align: "left", format: variableLabel },
  { key: "n_obs", label: "Observations" },
  ...flagValues.map((flag) => ({
    key: flagKey(flag),
    label: flagHeading(flag),
    title: flagTitle(flag),
    format: flagUnit === "Observations"
      ? undefined
      : (value, row) => app.formatSmallShare(value, row.n_obs)
  })),
  { key: "report", label: "Regional report", align: "left", render: (_, row) => reportLink(row) }
]) : html``
```

```{ojs}
meta ? app.analysisFigure(
  "input_flags_shares",
  "The observations each product flags other than 1 (good), as a share of all its observations, grouped the way the site reads them: bad (3, 4, 6, 7), no flag (0 for no QC performed, 9 for a missing value, or none), and usable values marked otherwise (2 probably good, 5 changed, 8 interpolated). The label is the total. Flag 1 is the rest of each product, too large to draw beside them.",
  "Stacked bars per product and variable of the share of observations with an input flag other than 1."
) : html``
```

## Against the regional reports

The regional reports count the same observations with two differences.
They file an observation the input gives no flag under 9 (missing value),
and they keep only profiles whose position is flagged good, which drops a
profile with no position flag at all. This site keeps those profiles: the
conversion dropped profiles whose position was flagged bad, and a missing
flag is no evidence of that. The table counts the observations both ways;
the last column is what the report shows.

```{ojs}
positionRows = flags
  ? [...flags.reduce((byKey, r) => {
      const key = `${r.dataset_id}|${r.variable}`;
      const row = byKey.get(key) ?? {
        dataset_id: r.dataset_id, variable: r.variable,
        n_obs: 0, n_no_position: 0, n_none: 0
      };
      row.n_obs += r.n_obs;
      if (r.has_position_qc === false) row.n_no_position += r.n_obs;
      else if (r.original_flag === null) row.n_none += r.n_obs;
      byKey.set(key, row);
      return byKey;
    }, new Map()).values()]
      .map((r) => ({ ...r, n_report: r.n_obs - r.n_no_position }))
      .sort((a, b) => byDataset(a, b) || byVariable(a, b))
  : []
meta ? table(positionRows, [
  { key: "dataset_id", label: "Product", align: "left", format: name },
  { key: "variable", label: "Variable", align: "left", format: variableLabel },
  { key: "n_obs", label: "Observations here" },
  { key: "n_no_position", label: "No position flag", title: "Observations of profiles with no position_qc, which the reports leave out" },
  { key: "no_position_share", label: "Share", format: (_, r) => app.formatSmallShare(r.n_no_position, r.n_obs) },
  { key: "n_none", label: "No flag, counted as 9", title: "Observations with no input flag, in profiles the reports keep; the reports file them under 9" },
  { key: "n_report", label: "By the reports' rule", title: "Observations of profiles with a position flag: the total of the report's table" },
  { key: "report", label: "Regional report", align: "left", render: (_, row) => reportLink(row) }
]) : html``
```

Counted by the reports' rule, the flags here matched each report's table
value for value when this page was written. Where a product is off by a
few observations, a profile lies on the edge of the report's region box:
inside it for the conversion, just outside it for the report.
